issues.legal_issue: Disputes arising from several agreements for one commercial project may be referred together to arbitration where the agreements are integral to a principal agreement containing an arbitration clause, despite the absence of a clause in an ancillary agreement.
material_facts: The parties had entered into four agreements concerning the procurement, installation and leasing of equipment for a single solar power project.
The principal equipment lease agreement contained an arbitration clause, while the sale and purchase agreement did not.

The supply, installation and sale agreements expressly contemplated that equipment would be supplied for onward lease to the project operator, and the lease agreement referred to those suppliers and allocated delivery and installation responsibilities.
The applicants sought reference of the disputes in the suit to arbitration, and the suit concerned disputes arising from the interconnected transactions.
issues.conclusion: The agreements were interconnected parts of a single commercial transaction, so the disputes and the parties to the four agreements were referred to arbitration.
issues.legal_principle: Section 8 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, as amended in 2015, requires reference where a valid arbitration agreement prima facie exists, notwithstanding prior judgments or orders. The amendment includes persons claiming through or under a party and confines the court’s inquiry at this stage to whether prima facie no valid arbitration agreement exists. Applying Chloro Controls India Private Limited v. Severn Trent Water Purification Inc. (2013) 1 SCC 641, parties to a composite transaction may be referred together where the agreements have a common subject matter and performance of the principal agreement depends on ancillary agreements. Sukanya Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Jayesh H. Pandya (2003) 5 SCC 531 did not bar reference on these facts because the agreements and parties were integral to one commercial project, rather than requiring an impermissible division of unrelated causes of action.

predicates.section_8_reference_application_in_suit: A party to a suit applied for the disputes to be referred to arbitration under an arbitration agreement.
predicates.principal_agreement_has_arbitration_clau: The parties entered into a principal agreement for the commercial transaction that contains an arbitration clause.
predicates.agreements_form_one_commercial_project: The parties used several agreements to carry out a single commercial project.
predicates.ancillary_agreements_are_integrally_conn: The ancillary agreements provide for steps, supplies or responsibilities needed to perform the principal agreement.

issues.definition: When a party seeks arbitration in a suit and the principal agreement contains an arbitration clause, disputes and parties under ancillary agreements forming an integral part of the same commercial project are referred together to arbitration.

issues.legal_issue: Allegations of fraud do not by themselves justify refusing arbitration when they are not serious and complex enough to require court determination and can be examined by the arbitrator.
material_facts: The plaintiffs alleged fraud and misrepresentation in connection with the equipment purchase and lease transactions.
The allegations against the appellants included that they induced the plaintiffs to pay a higher price for equipment.
A criminal complaint had resulted in a registered case, and proceedings concerning that case remained pending.
The commercial agreements contained arbitration clauses, and the court found that the allegations were not so serious as to prevent reference and could be examined by the arbitrator.
issues.conclusion: The fraud allegations did not justify refusing reference to arbitration; the arbitrator could examine them.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 8 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, mere allegations of fraud do not nullify an arbitration agreement. Ayyasamy v. A. Paramasivam (2016) 10 SCC 386 holds that reference may be refused only where the allegations are serious and complicated, amount to a virtual case of criminal offence, and are more appropriately determined by a court after appraisal of evidence. The court must also give commercial agreements a sense of business efficacy; an arbitrator may examine allegations that do not meet that serious-and-complicated threshold.

rule.if: section_8_reference_application_in_suit and arbitration_agreement_covers_dispute and fraud_is_alleged and not serious_complex_fraud_requires_court_determination

issues.definition: If arbitration is sought for a covered dispute and the fraud allegations do not require court determination because of their serious and complex nature, the allegations do not prevent arbitration.

issues.legal_issue: Interim lease payments may be ordered pending arbitration to protect a party’s interests where rent is alleged to be unpaid and related shareholdings have been transferred.
material_facts: The respondents asserted that lease rentals had not been paid under the equipment lease.
The court noted that the relevant company had transferred its shareholdings in solar power units.

The disputes were referred to arbitration, and the court directed payment of arrears and continuing lease rent until the arbitration was disposed of, without prejudice to the parties’ positions and subject to the arbitration’s outcome.
issues.conclusion: The appellants were directed to pay the lease arrears and continuing lease rent pending the arbitration, without prejudice to the parties’ contentions and subject to the final outcome.
issues.legal_principle: To protect the respondents’ interests until the arbitrator resolved the dispute, the Court ordered interim payment of lease rent in light of the asserted default and the transfer of shareholdings. The payments were made without prejudice to either side’s contentions and subject to the final outcome of arbitration.

issues.definition: When a commercial dispute is referred to arbitration, rent nonpayment is asserted, and related shareholdings have been transferred, interim lease-rent payments may be required pending the arbitration.
